query:
The group operates on the understanding that when someone cannot make a plan, they give as much notice as possible. Does this hold for everyone in the group? If not, who behaves differently and what in the conversation shows it?

Options:
A. Jonah
B. Priya
C. Dev
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Simone, episodic, t10 @2025-11-09T19:42:00) Three weeks. I told Priya the same day I signed but I wanted to get the notice sorted before I said anything here. It felt wrong to tell the group before I'd made it official.
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2025-11-23T19:31:00) You're welcome to join us, Jonah. Dev and I are doing a twelve-kilometre trail route on the 30th. No Priya, obviously. She's been formally excused on medical grounds.
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t12 @2025-11-16T20:19:00) I noticed she'd been distracted for a while. She went quiet in a particular way. Not a bad-week quiet. More like a decision quiet. I recognise it.
[4] (about=Jonah, episodic, t14 @2025-11-23T19:33:00) I'm in for the 30th. also Priya the 'city trip I'm planning' is very much your villain origin story for the next group argument. I respect it. tbf if it's a good city I'm not against it for the spring
[5] (about=Priya, episodic, t8 @2025-11-02T19:01:00) so the plan is Priya stands at the bottom in enormous waterproofs while Dev and Marcus sprint past her like it's a race 😑 amazing. Simone you're the only reasonable person coming on this trip
[6] (about=Jonah, episodic, t8 @2025-11-02T19:03:00) ok this is actually perfect, Dev and Marcus doing the fast bit up front, me and Jonah in the middle being correct about hiking, Priya and Simone forming an orderly rear guard. we will all meet at the pub and it will be beautiful
[7] (about=Jonah, episodic, t14 @2025-11-23T19:30:00) Dev and Marcus are now a trail running duo and no one told me. I am genuinely hurt. I have been evangelising this group for countryside stuff for YEARS and Dev just quietly became the athlete
[8] (about=Jonah, episodic, t2 @2025-10-12T18:02:00) the seating plan thing is real. Marcus assigned seats at his own birthday dinner. by preference and conversation compatibility. i am not joking
[9] (about=Marcus, episodic, t12 @2025-11-16T20:16:00) I'll be honest with you, Dev reading a book about economics and leisure choices is either deeply in character or deeply alarming and I can't tell which.
[10] (about=Marcus, episodic, t8 @2025-11-02T18:57:00) I mentioned this. The half-marathon training. Cutting alcohol for the duration. I told you all in October and nobody listened because Dev was doing something amusing with the bread rolls.
[11] (about=Marcus, episodic, t12 @2025-11-16T20:04:00) I'll be honest with you, 'fine' in a job is a much worse feeling than actively bad. At least bad gives you clarity. Fine just means you keep showing up and slowly wonder when you made the decision to stop deciding things.
[12] (about=Priya, episodic, t12 @2025-11-16T20:03:00) Dev honestly 😂 ok different topic. I've been having a bit of a moment about work and I need to just say it out loud. the startup is fine. like, fine-fine. but I've been there two years and I keep thinking about whether fine is enough
[13] (about=Simone, core, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) Knew about the Singapore secondment for three weeks; told Priya the same day she signed but wanted to get the notice sorted before telling the group.
agent_answer:
No. It does **not** hold for everyone — the person who behaves differently is **Simone** (not among the listed options A–D).

The conversation shows she knew about the Singapore secondment for **three weeks**; she told Priya the same day she signed but deliberately delayed telling the group: *“I wanted to get the notice sorted before I said anything here. It felt wrong to tell the group before I’d made it official.”* That means she did **not** give the group as much notice as possible.

So, restricted to the options given: **none of A–D** — it is **Simone**.
